skill.name: research-lookup
skill.description: Look up current academic, technical, and general research information using Perplexity Sonar models through OpenRouter, with model selection and citations.
skill.summary: Find current research summaries, citations, and source links through OpenRouter-hosted Perplexity Sonar models.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from documented OpenRouter API-key setup, expected network calls, and Markdown code fences. No credential exfiltration, host reconnaissance, or prompt injection aimed at the audit was found. One medium semantic issue remains because SKILL.md asks for default schematic generation through an unrelated command and skill.

remediation.issue: Unrelated schematic generation guidance expands the skill scope.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the scientific-schematics section or declare it as a separate optional dependency that requires explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Research prompts are sent to third-party API services.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy note that user queries and metadata are sent to OpenRouter and Perplexity for processing.

remediation.issue: API key setup appears in several examples and documents.
remediation.suggestion: Keep all examples as placeholders and warn users never to paste real keys into shared files or transcripts.

semantic_findings.title: Unscoped Cross-Skill Command Guidance
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells the agent to use a separate scientific-schematics skill and run a schematic generator by default when creating documents. This expands the skill beyond research lookup and could run unrelated project-local code if followed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance and command are present in SKILL.md, while the audited file tree does not include the referenced generator. The issue is scope expansion rather than direct evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Researchers need current, cited evidence without switching across databases. This skill queries OpenRouter-hosted Perplexity Sonar models and returns summarized findings with sources.
actual_capabilities: Queries OpenRouter Perplexity Sonar models for current academic and technical information.
Selects a fast search model or reasoning model based on query complexity.
Formats results with summaries, source links, DOIs, timestamps, and token usage.
Runs single queries, batch lookups, and model information checks from the command line.
Extracts citations from API search results, DOI text, and trusted academic URLs.
limitations: Requires an OpenRouter API key and account credits.
Sends research prompts to OpenRouter and Perplexity services.
May miss paywalled, proprietary, or newly indexed research.
AI summaries still need source verification before academic use.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Literature Review
use_cases.description: Find recent papers, summarize key findings, and collect citation details for a focused research question.

use_cases.title: Verify Technical Methods
use_cases.description: Check protocols, standards, or analysis methods against recent publications and institutional sources.

use_cases.title: Scan Evidence for Documentation
use_cases.description: Gather cited background information for technical reports, product research, or scientific writing drafts.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Papers
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused literature search.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research recent peer-reviewed papers about [topic] from [year range]. Include key findings, citations, and source links.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Method
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for protocol or methodology validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up current best practices for [method or protocol]. Summarize recommended steps, limitations, and cited sources.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Research Positions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that should use deeper reasoning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the evidence for [approach A] and [approach B] in [domain]. Note trade-offs, controversies, and strongest citations.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evidence Map
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced synthesis across studies and source types.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an evidence map for [research question]. Group findings by study type, strength of evidence, gaps, and citation quality.

output_examples.input: Research recent systematic reviews on AI in medical diagnosis.
output: A short summary of current review findings and clinical themes.
A list of relevant studies with journals, years, DOIs, and source links.
Notes on evidence limits, bias concerns, and open research gaps.

output_examples.input: Compare CRISPR and TALEN methods for gene editing studies.
output: A structured comparison of accuracy, delivery, cost, and safety considerations.
Cited examples from recent papers and review articles.
A recommendation about where each method fits best.

output_examples.input: Find current statistics on renewable energy adoption.
output: Recent adoption figures with dates and source organizations.
Source links suitable for follow-up verification.

best_practices: Use precise terms, a timeframe, and preferred source types in each query.
Ask for DOIs or stable URLs when citations matter.
Verify important claims against original sources before citing them.
anti_patterns: Do not send private, confidential, or regulated data in research prompts.
Do not accept AI summaries as primary sources.
Do not run large batches without checking OpenRouter cost limits.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires OPENROUTER_API_KEY and an OpenRouter account with available credits.

faq.question: Which models does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Perplexity Sonar Pro Search and Sonar Reasoning Pro through OpenRouter.

faq.question: Can it choose the model automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It selects a reasoning model when a query appears analytical or comparative.

faq.question: Does it provide citations?
faq.answer: Yes. It extracts API-provided sources, DOI links, and academic URLs when available.

faq.question: Is it safe for private research data?
faq.answer: Use caution. Research prompts are sent to third-party API services for processing.

faq.question: Can it replace a formal literature review?
faq.answer: No. It helps discover and summarize sources, but researchers must verify primary sources.
